title: A SLAVE IN A STRANGE LAND

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt. Potiphar, an Egyptian who was one of Pharaoh's officials, the captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there." - Gen 39:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the long detour into Judah's story, the narrative returns to Joseph — and it finds him at the bottom. He has been "taken down to Egypt," torn from his family, and sold like property to an Egyptian official. Yesterday he was the favored son in an ornate robe; now he is a foreign slave, bought and paid for, with no rights and no say in his own life.

It would be hard to imagine a lower place to begin. Joseph is far from home, stripped of everything, at the mercy of strangers in a land whose language and gods he does not share. If ever a young man had reason to believe God had abandoned him, this was it.

Yet this is exactly where God's quiet work begins. As we will see, the Lord had not forgotten Joseph, and this lowly slave-market would become the doorway to a purpose greater than Joseph could imagine. God often begins His deepest work in the lowest places.

If you feel that life has brought you "down" — to a place of loss, powerlessness, or exile from all that was familiar — take heart from where Joseph's story now stands. The bottom is not beyond God's reach. Some of the Lord's greatest purposes have started in the humblest, hardest of circumstances. God is not finished with you where you are.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I ever felt life bring me "down" to a place of loss or powerlessness?
2. Do I believe God can begin His work even in the lowest places?
3. Where do I need to trust that the bottom is not beyond God's reach?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when life brings me low, remind me that You have not abandoned me. Begin Your work in my hard places, and help me to trust that the bottom is not beyond Your reach. Amen.
